title: Are boys taller than girls in these schools?
description: The mean heights of boys and girls in grades six, seven and eight of two schools are compared grade by grade and boys against girls. Keeko thinks girls are taller than boys because they lead in one grade.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare like with like using the printed means, and do not turn one grade of one school into a rule. Watch for students who generalise from the first row they read.

source: Using the printed means, compare the two schools grade by grade, and boys with girls in each school
video_script.why: The child can read a mean from a dot plot and now compares means across groups.
video_script.substitution: The book's own dot plots of heights of boys and girls of grades six, seven and eight in two schools, read through their printed means.
video_script.anchor: Mean heights in cm. First school, boys then girls: grade 6: 134.8, 137.78; grade 7: 141.8, 141.83; grade 8: 149.35, 147.81. Second school: grade 6: 149.84, 150.2; grade 7: 156.14, 155.41; grade 8: 156.14, 156.83.
video_script.wrong_move: Reads one grade of one school, sees girls ahead, and treats it as a rule for every grade.
video_script.payoff_line: The second school is taller in every grade, but boys against girls keeps changing.

final_answer.value: The second school is taller in every grade; boys against girls changes from grade to grade, so no general claim follows
final_answer.spoken: the second school is taller in every grade; boys against girls changes from grade to grade, so no general claim follows

maths_rules: grade 6 boys: 149.84 - 134.8 = 15.04 cm taller in the second school
every grade, boys and girls, has a higher mean in the second school
first school: girls ahead in grade 6 (137.78 against 134.8), nearly equal in grade 7 (141.83 against 141.8), boys ahead in grade 8 (149.35 against 147.81)
second school: girls ahead in grades 6 and 8, boys ahead in grade 7
video_script.design: One idea: compare means like with like, one grade at a time. The twelve means sit in the anchor; on the board one gap is found, then boys and girls are compared in each school.

<bookmark mark='m5'/>Check the other five groups the same way. Each mean is higher in the second school.
